title: Retention policy API payload examples + migration notes (v1 -> v1.1)
content:
Context
- This doc is a grab-bag of payload examples we’ve been using in dev + in security review rehearsals. It is intentionally “copy/paste friendly” and includes expected validation failures.
- Applies to retention policy service (control plane). Policies are evaluated in control plane and pushed to data-plane purge jobs via config + evaluation cache invalidation (see ADR-017).

Terminology (quick)
- data_class: logical bucket of stored data we retain/purge (request_logs, audit_logs, traces, metrics, artifacts).
- ttl_days: requested time-to-live (days). Enforced by purge jobs (idempotent deletes) and/or storage TTL where supported.
- purge_semantics:
  - hard_delete: delete rows/objects permanently on purge execution.
  - soft_delete: mark deleted; hard delete later (not supported for v1/v1.1 by default; included for forward compatibility).
- legal_hold:
  - enabled: blocks purge for affected data_classes; does NOT increase collection.
  - reason + ticket required for audit trail.

Endpoint summary (current)
- GET  /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/retention-policy
- PUT  /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/retention-policy  (upsert)
- POST /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/retention-policy:validate
- GET  /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/retention-policy:history
- GET  /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/retention-policy:export  (compliance pack attachment)

Notes on schema versions
v1 (GA target for early design partners)
- Top-level: policy_version, effective_at, data_classes[]
- Each data_class entry: name, enabled, ttl_days
- No per-region overrides
- No structured legal_hold object (early prototype used boolean “hold” in some internal payloads; do not rely on it)

v1.1 (adds explicit overrides + legal hold + policy metadata)
- Adds policy_metadata object (change_note, requested_by, source)
- Adds overrides[] for region + tier specific TTLs (with strict validation and precedence)
- Adds legal_hold object per data_class (and optional global hold)
- Adds explicit purge_semantics (hard_delete only currently accepted)

IMPORTANT: API accepts policy_version=“1.0” and “1.1”. If omitted, default is “1.0” for backwards compatibility UNTIL we flip the default in Phase 2.

----------------------------------------
Example 1: Get policy (no policy set yet)
REQUEST
GET /v1/tenants/tnt_6f3d2d/retention-policy

RESPONSE (200)
{
  "tenant_id": "tnt_6f3d2d",
  "policy_version": "1.0",
  "policy_state": "DEFAULTS_APPLIED",
  "effective_at": "2025-03-01T00:00:00Z",
  "data_classes": [
    {"name": "audit_logs", "enabled": true, "ttl_days": 365},
    {"name": "request_logs", "enabled": true, "ttl_days": 30},
    {"name": "traces", "enabled": true, "ttl_days": 14},
    {"name": "metrics", "enabled": true, "ttl_days": 14},
    {"name": "artifacts", "enabled": false, "ttl_days": 0}
  ],
  "last_updated_at": "2025-03-01T00:00:00Z"
}

Notes
- policy_state=DEFAULTS_APPLIED means tenant hasn’t explicitly set anything; defaults are derived from product tier and logging mode.
- artifacts: default disabled until we finalize scope for eval datasets / prompt sets retention.

----------------------------------------
Example 2: Upsert v1 policy (simple)
REQUEST
PUT /v1/tenants/tnt_6f3d2d/retention-policy
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "policy_version": "1.0",
  "effective_at": "2025-03-10T00:00:00Z",
  "data_classes": [
    {"name": "audit_logs", "enabled": true, "ttl_days": 400},
    {"name": "request_logs", "enabled": true, "ttl_days": 7},
    {"name": "traces", "enabled": true, "ttl_days": 7},
    {"name": "metrics", "enabled": true, "ttl_days": 30}
  ]
}

RESPONSE (200)
{
  "tenant_id": "tnt_6f3d2d",
  "policy_version": "1.0",
  "policy_state": "CUSTOM",
  "effective_at": "2025-03-10T00:00:00Z",
  "data_classes": [
    {"name": "audit_logs", "enabled": true, "ttl_days": 400},
    {"name": "request_logs", "enabled": true, "ttl_days": 7},
    {"name": "traces", "enabled": true, "ttl_days": 7},
    {"name": "metrics", "enabled": true, "ttl_days": 30},
    {"name": "artifacts", "enabled": false, "ttl_days": 0}
  ],
  "warnings": [
    "request_logs ttl_days=7 may reduce incident triage capability; ensure on-call runbook has break-glass steps."
  ],
  "last_updated_at": "2025-03-10T00:00:12Z"
}

Notes
- Server will normalize: include all known data classes (missing ones are filled with defaults).
- warnings is best-effort; not a blocker.

----------------------------------------
Example 3: Validate-only endpoint (use in Console)
REQUEST
POST /v1/tenants/tnt_6f3d2d/retention-policy:validate

{
  "policy_version": "1.1",
  "effective_at": "2025-03-12T00:00:00Z",
  "policy_metadata": {
    "change_note": "Shorten request logs for HIPAA workload",
    "requested_by": "user_82c9",
    "source": "console"
  },
  "data_classes": [
    {
      "name": "request_logs",
      "enabled": true,
      "ttl_days": 3,
      "purge_semantics": "hard_delete",
      "legal_hold": {"enabled": false}
    }
  ],
  "overrides": [
    {
      "match": {"region": "us-east-1"},
      "data_classes": [{"name": "request_logs", "ttl_days": 7}]
    }
  ]
}

RESPONSE (200)
{
  "valid": true,
  "normalized_policy": "(omitted here; mirrors PUT response)"
}

Notes
- validate endpoint performs the same validation + normalization as PUT, but does not persist.

----------------------------------------
Example 4: v1.1 policy with global legal hold + override precedence
REQUEST
PUT /v1/tenants/tnt_6f3d2d/retention-policy

{
  "policy_version": "1.1",
  "effective_at": "2025-03-15T00:00:00Z",
  "policy_metadata": {
    "change_note": "Enterprise security review: set explicit TTLS + add legal hold procedure",
    "requested_by": "user_3a14",
    "source": "api"
  },
  "global": {
    "legal_hold": {
      "enabled": false
    }
  },
  "data_classes": [
    {
      "name": "audit_logs",
      "enabled": true,
      "ttl_days": 365,
      "purge_semantics": "hard_delete",
      "legal_hold": {
        "enabled": true,
        "reason": "Regulatory inquiry - preserve access logs",
        "ticket": "LEGAL-2194"
      }
    },
    {
      "name": "request_logs",
      "enabled": true,
      "ttl_days": 14,
      "purge_semantics": "hard_delete",
      "legal_hold": {"enabled": false}
    },
    {
      "name": "traces",
      "enabled": true,
      "ttl_days": 7,
      "purge_semantics": "hard_delete",
      "legal_hold": {"enabled": false}
    },
    {
      "name": "metrics",
      "enabled": true,
      "ttl_days": 30,
      "purge_semantics": "hard_delete",
      "legal_hold": {"enabled": false}
    }
  ],
  "overrides": [
    {
      "match": {"region": "eu-west-1"},
      "data_classes": [
        {"name": "request_logs", "ttl_days": 7},
        {"name": "traces", "ttl_days": 3}
      ]
    },
    {
      "match": {"region": "us-east-1"},
      "data_classes": [
        {"name": "request_logs", "ttl_days": 30}
      ]
    }
  ]
}

Notes on precedence (as implemented in evaluator tests)
1) Base policy data_classes apply globally
2) Region override (match.region) applies on top for that region
3) If in future we add tier overrides, precedence will be: base < tier < region < tier+region (most specific)
4) legal_hold: if enabled at any applicable layer, purge is blocked for that data_class in that scope

----------------------------------------
Example 5: Export policy for compliance pack attachment
REQUEST
GET /v1/tenants/tnt_6f3d2d/retention-policy:export?format=json

RESPONSE (200)
{
  "export_version": "retention_policy_export@2025-03-01",
  "generated_at": "2025-03-20T18:22:10Z",
  "tenant_id": "tnt_6f3d2d",
  "policy": {
    "policy_version": "1.1",
    "effective_at": "2025-03-15T00:00:00Z",
    "data_classes": "(same as stored)",
    "overrides": "(same as stored)",
    "policy_metadata": {
      "last_change_note": "Enterprise security review: set explicit TTLS + add legal hold procedure",
      "last_updated_by": "user_3a14",
      "last_updated_at": "2025-03-15T00:00:08Z"
    }
  }
}

Notes
- Export is used by audit-log-exporter bundling (see exporter PR-627).
- export_version is versioned independently of policy_version so we can evolve report pack outputs without changing policy evaluation.

----------------------------------------
Validation + error messages (examples)

1) ttl_days below minimum
REQUEST
PUT /v1/tenants/tnt_6f3d2d/retention-policy

{
  "policy_version": "1.1",
  "effective_at": "2025-03-15T00:00:00Z",
  "data_classes": [
    {"name": "audit_logs", "enabled": true, "ttl_days": 1, "purge_semantics": "hard_delete"}
  ]
}

RESPONSE (400)
{
  "error": {
    "code": "RETENTION_VALIDATION_ERROR",
    "message": "ttl_days out of bounds for data_class=audit_logs",
    "details": [
      "audit_logs.ttl_days must be between 90 and 2555 for tier=Dedicated"
    ]
  }
}

Note
- Bounds vary by product tier + logging mode. In Private, upper bound may be “unbounded” only when customer-managed storage TTL is in place (still debated; expect to keep an upper cap in v1.1).

2) Unsupported purge_semantics
REQUEST
{
  "policy_version": "1.1",
  "effective_at": "2025-03-15T00:00:00Z",
  "data_classes": [
    {"name": "request_logs", "enabled": true, "ttl_days": 7, "purge_semantics": "soft_delete"}
  ]
}

RESPONSE (400)
{
  "error": {
    "code": "RETENTION_VALIDATION_ERROR",
    "message": "Unsupported purge_semantics",
    "details": [
      "request_logs.purge_semantics must be one of: hard_delete"
    ]
  }
}

3) Overrides with unknown region
REQUEST
{
  "policy_version": "1.1",
  "effective_at": "2025-03-15T00:00:00Z",
  "data_classes": [{"name": "metrics", "enabled": true, "ttl_days": 14, "purge_semantics": "hard_delete"}],
  "overrides": [{"match": {"region": "moon-1"}, "data_classes": [{"name": "metrics", "ttl_days": 7}]}]
}

RESPONSE (400)
{
  "error": {
    "code": "RETENTION_VALIDATION_ERROR",
    "message": "Invalid override match",
    "details": [
      "overrides[0].match.region must be a supported region for tenant (supported: us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1)"
    ]
  }
}

4) Attempt to enable request_logs when logging is disabled
Scenario
- Tenant is configured with logging_mode=DISABLED (no request/response logs stored).

REQUEST
{
  "policy_version": "1.1",
  "effective_at": "2025-03-15T00:00:00Z",
  "data_classes": [{"name": "request_logs", "enabled": true, "ttl_days": 30, "purge_semantics": "hard_delete"}]
}

RESPONSE (409)
{
  "error": {
    "code": "RETENTION_CONFLICT",
    "message": "request_logs retention cannot be enabled because logging is disabled for this tenant",
    "details": [
      "Set logging_mode to STANDARD or SAMPLING before enabling request_logs retention."
    ]
  }
}

5) Legal hold missing ticket/reason
REQUEST
{
  "policy_version": "1.1",
  "effective_at": "2025-03-15T00:00:00Z",
  "data_classes": [
    {"name": "audit_logs", "enabled": true, "ttl_days": 365, "purge_semantics": "hard_delete", "legal_hold": {"enabled": true}}
  ]
}

RESPONSE (400)
{
  "error": {
    "code": "RETENTION_VALIDATION_ERROR",
    "message": "legal_hold enabled but missing required fields",
    "details": [
      "audit_logs.legal_hold.reason is required when legal_hold.enabled=true",
      "audit_logs.legal_hold.ticket is required when legal_hold.enabled=true"
    ]
  }
}

6) Permissions / RBAC
- Only Security Admin / Org Admin can edit retention policies in Console; API requires scope=retention_policy:write.

RESPONSE (403)
{
  "error": {
    "code": "FORBIDDEN",
    "message": "Missing required permission: retention_policy:write"
  }
}

----------------------------------------
Migration notes (v1 -> v1.1)

What changed (high signal)
- Added: policy_metadata, overrides, purge_semantics, legal_hold object
- v1 payloads are still accepted, stored as v1, and normalized with defaults.
- Console will begin writing v1.1 once feature flag RETENTION_SCHEMA_V1_1 is enabled (per-tenant rollout).

Recommended migration approach
1) Read existing v1 policy
2) Write v1.1 equivalent policy:
   - For each data_class, carry over enabled + ttl_days
   - Set purge_semantics="hard_delete"
   - Set legal_hold.enabled=false unless hold is active via separate workflow
   - Add policy_metadata.change_note
3) If customer needs per-region deviations, add overrides (keep minimal)
4) Validate (call :validate), then persist (PUT)

Mapping table (v1 -> v1.1)
- v1.data_classes[].ttl_days -> v1.1.data_classes[].ttl_days (unchanged)
- v1 has no legal_hold -> v1.1.legal_hold.enabled=false by default
- v1 has no purge_semantics -> v1.1.purge_semantics=hard_delete by default

Backward compatibility gotchas
- If policy_version omitted: current default is 1.0. Console MUST specify 1.1 explicitly once enabled.
- Some internal proto payloads used ttl_hours (never shipped). Not supported. Expect RETENTION_VALIDATION_ERROR.

----------------------------------------
Common edge cases (from Slack + tickets)

Edge case: “disable logging” but still wants audit logs
- Expected: audit_logs are independent of request logging and can remain enabled.
- Make sure tenant config doesn’t couple them. Validation should only block request_logs/traces derived from request pipeline.

Edge case: TTL lag / purge backlog
- Not an API issue but shows up in customer reports.
- When a customer changes ttl_days from 30 -> 7, the system will not instant-delete; purge job will work backlog. We should communicate: "enforced within N hours" with SLO and expose ttl_lag_seconds.

Edge case: lowering TTL below incident response minimum
- We allow but warn (non-blocking). Break-glass is via incident exception workflow; do not promise we can recover purged logs.

----------------------------------------
TODO / open questions (keep updated)
- Do we allow ttl_days=0 with enabled=true as shorthand for “disable + purge immediately”? Current stance: NO (force enabled=false).
- artifacts data class scope: include eval datasets? prompt sets? model artifacts? (likely Phase 2/3)
- Private deployments: do we treat upper bounds differently when customer uses object store lifecycle policies?
- Error message consistency: ensure details[] are stable (Console tests rely on substring matching today; we should fix that).

Last notes to self (Benji)
- Re-check min/max bounds in schema doc before sharing payloads with Solutions Eng. We had at least one mismatch last week between Dedicated and Hosted bounds.
- When we flip default schema to 1.1, make sure legacy clients that do PUT without policy_version don’t “accidentally downgrade” a 1.1 policy. Likely need server-side guard: reject PUT v1 if stored is v1.1 unless explicitly policy_version=1.0 + allow_downgrade flag (TBD).
